name: Drawquarium
lang: English, French, German, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Russian
short: Draw your very own fish and build a cozy little aquarium. And if you like, set it as your animated desktop wallpaper! Watch your drawings come to life. Feed them, raise them and collect golden scales to unlock new decorations. There's also some handy tools to help you focus and unwind.
about: Hi, I'm Kaleb! I work as a 3D artist in the film industry, but my heart kept pulling me toward a small, very personal game idea. One of the reasons I started developing this game was that I wanted to bring my children’s drawings to life 💖.      Drawquarium is a relaxing aquarium sandbox where your drawings come to life!  Draw your own fish and plants, feed them, raise them, and collect golden fish scales to unlock new decorations and tools. Create your own cozy little underwater world and bring it to your desktop as an animated wallpaper!     And don't worry, you don't have to be an artist to create something beautiful! You can always choose from a variety of ready-made fish and simply enjoy watching your little aquarium come to life.              Draw Your Own Fish COMPANIONS   Draw anything you want and watch your creations come to life inside your aquarium. Start with simple shapes, use templates for a little inspiration, or get as creative as you like. There are no rules, just you and your imagination!            When you place new creatures in your fish tank, they will interact with the others, forming friendships, rivalries and even relationships. They can become enemies and quibble or find their soulmate and have cute little babies 🥰.               Decorate With Your Own Plants   Any decent aquarium will need an abundance of thriving plants. Create the perfect habitat by drawing your own vegetation and placing it wherever you want. Of course, if you’d rather be drawing sea mines or skyscrapers… Who are we to stop you?          Wallpaper mode!  Miss your babies whenever you go and close the game? Simply turn on the Desktop Wallpaper Mode and all of your creations will stay right there with you. Whether you’re crunching numbers for the boss or browsing a forum, you can observe, feed and play with your fish right there on your desktop.           Unlock Limitless Customization   Change the way the sand looks, customize the lighting, and place decorative rocks, driftwood and more. Your aquarium is a tiny living world, filled with creatures made and cared for by you.            Your Cozy Little Space to Focus & Unwind   Journal your thoughts, organize your day with a task manager, or use the timer to stay focused. Customize your clock and set your aquarium as an animated desktop wallpaper, so your little fish friends can keep you company while you work, study, or simply unwind.           Upload Your Own Drawings   Upload any PNG image and watch it become part of your aquarium! Whether it's your kid's latest masterpiece or something you created yourself.             Visit anytime     for a gentle, mindful break     ♥

short: Robotic arms sweep a steady pour of coins off your plateau. Unlock islands, conquer six realms and ascend for crystals in an idle game that sits on your desktop while you work or play.
about: Coins pour from a pipe and pile up on your plateau. Robotic arms swing through the heap and sweep them over the edge into their chutes, and every coin that falls in pays. That's the loop. Now make it bigger.  Click Pour to drop more coins, or unlock Auto Flow and let the pipe run on its own. Click fast and a boost multiplier builds up. Unlock up to six islands in each realm, each with its own arm, and upgrade each arm's speed, size, magnetism, lucky drops and critical hits. Bronze coins give way to silver, gold, platinum, diamond, emerald and ruby, each worth more than the last.                Six realms stand between you and the top, from Brass to Frost. Every realm has its own coins and islands, plus a rule that changes how it plays. Heavy Coins pour slowly but pay more, Sparkling Crits land often and hit hard, and Frozen Time makes boosts last longer. Move coins between realms at the Exchange. The realms you leave behind keep earning a share while you play another.  When a realm has earned enough, ascend. It starts over, pays out crystals and opens the next realm. Crystals go to the Crystal Shop: permanent upgrades that survive every ascension (more income, free islands, cheaper exchanges, the Auto-Pour ability) and one-off boosts like Gold Rush and Time Warp.  The whole thing runs as a small transparent widget on your desktop. Drag it wherever it fits and keep it on top if you like. It keeps earning while you work or play, and you can switch to fullscreen at any time.

name: SUSHI PARADE Demo
lang: English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Spanish - Latin America, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian
short: The demo of a conveyor belt sushi shop on your desktop. Plates pass in front of your windows, and clicks off the lane go through to your apps. Chefs make sushi, customers eat it, and coins come in. Fill a Sushi Dex of about 80 entries and lay out the lane your way.
about: A conveyor belt sushi shop on your desktop  SUSHI PARADE runs in a transparent window laid over your desktop, so the lane and its plates pass in front of whatever you have open. The game only takes clicks on its own parts: the lane, the characters, and any open menu. Click anywhere else and it goes straight to the app behind.  Want it out of the way? Run a single lane along one edge of the screen, or turn off Always on Top and let your other windows cover it.          A small shop that keeps itself busy  Chefs make sushi and send it down the lane. Customers come by, each with their own tastes, budget, and appetite, eat what they like, and pay in coins. You can click a plate to eat it yourself or carry it to someone. There is no way to fail.  When you feel like doing more:   Orders: accept the ticket above a customer's head and the chef makes that sushi first. Filling it pays extra coins and EXP.  Hand swap: as the game goes on, you can right-click the lane to change hands. Glutton vacuums up nearby plates, and Serving Hand sends a plate to a customer.  Time away: sales from up to 8 hours are waiting when you next open the game.   Small things happen, too. Empty plates pile up on the rack. A plate nobody eats grows wings and a halo and floats away. And Shari Ryman, who left a trading company to open this shop, sometimes murmurs, "…I still can't throw out my business cards."       About 80 entries to collect  The demo's Sushi Dex holds about 80 entries: sushi from Tuna (Lean) to Snow Crab, plus sides such as tea, juice, and sweets. Each entry comes with its own description and a comment from Shari.  New sushi opens up in Neta Dev ("neta" means the topping). Eat enough of one kind, save up coins, and the next comes within reach. Rarely, a plate comes by as Shiny and sells for more.       Make the lane your own  About 20 lane shapes unlock as the shop grows: one line along the bottom, an L, a small ring in the corner, a route through all four corners, and shapes with warps built in. Lane Skins such as Hinoki Flow and Choo-Choo Railway change the look. Invisible draws no belt at all, leaving only the plates moving across your desktop.  As the game goes on, Lane Craft lets you draw your own on a grid. The demo limits how many custom lanes you can keep. Each new lane uses a Craft Hammer: you get some when Lane Craft opens and more each day, and hammers can't be bought. You also get Glitch and Edge Warp parts, which send plates from one stretch to another on a Fixed layout. A Fixed layout works only at the screen size it was made on.       As the shop grows, you can also place furniture around the lane, such as a Noren Curtain, Red Lantern, Goldfish Bowl, or Cat on a Cushion, and a food sample of any sushi you have eaten many times.  Streaming and videos are welcome  Feel free to stream SUSHI PARADE or post videos of it. Monetization is fine, and there is no need to ask for permission. It also works nicely left running in the corner of a work-along or chatting stream. If you capture a window, turn on Streamer Mode in Settings to show the game as a normal window with a background.  Technical notes  SUSHI PARADE has no servers or accounts of its own and sends no analytics. It goes online only through the Steam client, for Steam Cloud saves and Steam's server clock (used for daily bonuses and limited-time events). Buttons that lead outside the game, such as the demo survey, open in your browser only when you press them. To tell whether a click should land on the game, it reads the cursor position; it does not monitor your keyboard.  Because the game layers a transparent window over your desktop, a small number of antivirus programs may warn about it on first launch. Overlays may also conflict with the anti-cheat software used by some online games, such as Vanguard or EasyAntiCheat, so we recommend quitting SUSHI PARADE before playing them. On macOS, Screen Recording permission is requested only if you use the Desktop

about: About This Game  Desktop Tiny Tides is a relaxing desktop fishing game that transforms your computer screen into an active aquatic world.  Fish swim freely across your desktop while you control a small fishing boat by dragging it wherever you want to go. Follow schools of fish, search for rare species, cast your line, and complete a timing-based fishing minigame to secure your catch.  The game runs directly on your desktop, allowing fish and your boat to travel across multiple monitors. You can keep the game open while doing other things or focus entirely on finding every species.  A Living Desktop Ecosystem  The fish are more than simple collectibles. They move around the desktop, form schools, avoid obstacles, react to your boat, flee from danger, and interact with other fish.  Some fish stay close to the bottom of the screen, while others travel in groups or hide near desktop icons. Larger predators may hunt smaller fish, and nearby fish can become frightened and escape.  Every fish has its own behavior, preferred time of day, size range, weight, and rarity.  144 Different Fish  Discover 144 different fish species ranging from common everyday catches to extremely rare mythical discoveries.  Fish can appear in several rarity levels:    Common    Uncommon    Rare    Epic    Legendary    Mythic    Each fish also has a randomly determined size and weight. Larger catches are physically bigger, more valuable, and harder to overlook as they swim across your desktop.  Your collection records every species you have caught. Undiscovered fish remain hidden as silhouettes until you successfully catch them.  Fish at Different Times of Day  Different species appear during different parts of the day.  The game uses your computer’s local time to determine whether it is morning, afternoon, evening, or night. Some fish may only appear during a specific period, encouraging you to return at different times to complete your collection.  Timing-Based Fishing  Casting is controlled by holding and releasing the mouse button. The longer you charge the cast, the farther your bobber travels.  Once a fish bites, a timing-based fishing minigame begins. Stop the rotating indicator inside the success zone to reel the fish closer. More valuable fish require greater precision and may need several successful rounds before they can be caught.  Fish rarity affects the difficulty, while equipped fishing equipment can improve your chances.  Upgrade Your Fishing Equipment  Earn coins from your catches and spend them on new equipment.  Fishing Rods  Better rods increase the size of the minigame success zone, making difficult fish easier to catch.  Bobbers  Improved bobbers increase your maximum casting distance, allowing you to reach fish farther away from your boat.  Lures  Lures reduce the number of successful minigame stages required to catch a fish. Powerful lures can instantly catch fish that would normally require several rounds.  Fishing Traps  Place draggable fishing traps around your desktop. When a fish swims into an active trap, it has a chance to be caught automatically. Different traps provide different catch probabilities.  Purchased equipment can be equipped directly through the shop and visually changes parts of your fishing setup.  Explore Your Entire Desktop  Your boat is not restricted to a traditional body of water. Drag it freely across the desktop and between connected monitors.  Fish can appear from every direction and continue swimming throughout the available desktop space. Move your boat closer to interesting fish, but approach carefully, as they may notice you and flee. name: My First Beehive
lang: English**
short: A slow, painted beekeeping game for the corner of your screen. Keep one hive of honeybees through a real year: watch the comb fill, find the queen, sell the honey, and spend it on the garden they fly out to. Nothing dies. It just keeps going while you work.
about: A hive on your desk, painted in acrylic My First Beehive is an idle beekeeping game built to sit beside your work. One glass-fronted observation hive, three frames of comb, and a garden out the back door. You look in when you like. The bees get on with it either way. A real year, at a gentle pace The colony follows the seasons of a Northern Virginia garden. A season is a week of your time. In spring the queen fills the comb with brood and the first honey arches over the top; in summer the foragers work the tulip poplar and the wildflowers; in fall the goldenrod comes in and the cluster draws together for winter. Leave for a fortnight and come back to the fortnight you missed, written in the journal. Everything on the comb is a bee doing something Watch a worker chew her way out of her cell and walk off pale. Find the queen - she is half again as long as the others, and she keeps to the brood. Put the magnifying glass on any cell and it tells you what is in it: an egg, a larva, capped honey, packed pollen. Foragers come home through the tube with pollen on their legs, the colour of whatever is flowering. Keep them, or just watch There are only a few things to do, and none of them is a chore. Harvest when there is honey to spare. Feed them if the stores run low. Treat for mites in the fall. Skip all of it and the hive is still there next spring, a little smaller. Nothing dies - a season you sit out costs you honey, and never the colony. Sell the honey. Spend it on the garden. Your honey is money. Every jar goes in the journal named for the flow it came from, and then you sell it and decide what it buys: another bed of flowers, the mite treatment that keeps the colony strong through the fall, or a tree - the expensive thing, bought perhaps once a year, that arrives as a sapling and takes seasons to fill out. And the garden pays you back. What is in bloom when the bees fly decides how much honey you get and what kind it is, so a bed planted this spring is next summer's harvest. A thin first year buys one more thing. A garden you have kept for years is a different hive altogether. A garden that moves Plant beds of coneflower, daisy, bee balm and black-eyed Susan, and the bees fly out to them. One breeze crosses the whole garden and every flower leans with it. Birds sing from the trees. It is always mid-afternoon. Where you put things is close to permanent, so the garden becomes a record of every choice you made. Painted, not rendered Every comb cell, every flower and every bee is a painting in acrylic, composited and moved by code. It looks like a picture because it is one. What is in the hive today   One observation hive, three frames, seen one at a time - lean in to the cells.   A real 364-day year at one season a week; it catches up on the time you were away.   The queen, the brood, the honey and the pollen, laid down the way a colony lays them.   A honey journal written in a real hand: a page a fortnight, every jar named for its flow.   Four things to do and no chores: harvest, feed, treat, check the stores. Skipping them costs honey, never the colony.   A real economy: sell your honey and spend it on flowers, on beekeeping supplies, and on trees that arrive as saplings and grow for years.   A garden that decides your harvest - what is flowering when the bees fly sets how much honey you get, and what kind.   Idle by design: it runs in a small window while you do something else.

about: Cosmo Corgis  Gather resources, get your upgrades, rescue corgis, and hop on your ship from planet to planet on the way home. Cosmo Corgis is a cozy desktop companion idler with ten planets, ten stranded corgis, and six personalities to keep you company while you work.  This is my first game release on Steam and I really hope you enjoy it!        Rescue the Corgi  Collect a corgi from each planet and make space for them on the ship that Scout crashed... again. Who gave Scout the astronaut his license? No action is needed from you. Scout handles the rescuing automatically.  Meet the Corgis         Ten rescued corgis, six personalities, and a colored space suit and backpack for each personality:   Mechanic, in yellow, welds beside the rocket with sparks and a little "Bzzzz."  Security, in blue, chases visiting wildlife with an oversized megaphone and amplified borks.  Mining, in amber, gathers resources with a backpack laser.  Lazy, in purple, unfolds a hover bed from its backpack and gets comfortable.  Chaos, in red, does zoomies and chases balls from its backpack launcher.  Clingy, in green, follows Scout and helps carry resources.   Your crew grows with every rescue. They take turns doing their thing, with occasional close-ups so you can enjoy the little moments.  Gather Resources  Scout gathers the resources needed to repair his ship and reach the next planet. This is an idler, so he does the hard work while you get on with yours—or sit back and watch him and the corgis entertain you.  Upgrade  Upgrade your axe to gather more wood, your pickaxe to gather more ore, and work toward Scout's laser rifle. Give his trailing storage cart more room so he can stay out longer, and expand the base storage to hold the haul. The default autopilot handles upgrades for you, or you can take charge of what to improve next.  Repair Your Ship         Scout's ship is what gets him from planet to planet. However, Scout is a terrible pilot and crash lands on each planet. He must build good safety systems because he comes out unscathed every time. Scout has to make more room for the corgi that you rescue on that planet, so it needed to come apart anyway. Right?  Fly to the Next Planet  Once Scout's ship is in tip top shape, it's time to crash into the next planet! Scout and his corgi companions blast off into the cosmos in search of the next planet on their way home, faceplant the rocket and start the process all over again!  Bring All of the Corgis Home  All of these corgis need some place to stay. Planet 10 brings all ten rescued corgis together for a reunion. Keep Scout and his gang in front of your other apps, or bring your windows forward and get back to work. Enjoy the peaceful music and the corgis barking as they play, or turn either off. Your choice.

short: A sliver of battlefield above your taskbar. While you work, your adventurer fights, loots, grows — and one day falls. The gear, the Soul Stones, and the story they leave behind carry the next one farther. An idle ARPG for your desktop, walking a fallen world to the edge of the map.
about: Adventurers fall. Their stories remain.  Desk Quest is an idle ARPG that lives in a thin, full-width strip right above your Windows taskbar. While you work, an adventurer is born, fights, grows — and one day falls. Standing on what they left behind, the next one walks a little farther.      A battlefield one sliver tall that never covers your work. Fighting, walking, and looting all take care of themselves. When the meeting starts, flip on  Work Mode  to quiet the effects and sound, or tuck the game into the tray — the adventure keeps going. Time spent with the game closed comes back as offline rewards. It's not a game you hide. It's a game you proudly leave running.      Every adventurer is born with a different face, different talents, a different temperament. At roadside altars, campfires, and strangers' graves, you can make the call — or let their nature decide. The fallen are kept in  the Archive , with their portrait, their story, and the time they spent on the road. Those who were first to do something are remembered with honors. And an adventurer who has walked far enough may lay down the road and live out their days in peace.      No chests. No "open" button. Gear drops where the monster falls, goes straight into your  Codex , and anything better gets equipped for you. Grades climb from Common all the way to Mythic, with sets to complete and gear to collect. Your Codex outlives every adventurer and readies the next one for the road. As for your favorite blade — enhance and enchant it as far as it will go.      The world ended once. No one remembers why. With the  Soul Stones  your adventurers leave behind, raise the ruined forge and workshops again, and build strength that passes down the bloodline. Your first adventurer is human — but the road doesn't end there. Some races you'll welcome through the Soul Shop, some you'll meet by chance on the road, and some wait only beyond the edge of the map.      No one has to walk alone. Pets hatch from eggs, and you won't know what's inside until it cracks open. Pets walk beside your adventurer and lend their strength in battle. In time, more of them can travel together. The Controls Are Yours  Auto-fire is not auto-win: move with WASD or arrow keys; press  Space  to dash through bullets or escape a boss's fire. Spend stardust to unlock Autopilot for movement; touch the controls and it yields. EVA speaks for tutorials and new situations, then gives you back the battlefield.     Stardust Is for Spending; Eight Weapons, All Clocked In  Spend stardust on 49 upgrades across  Fire ,  Orbs ,  Systems ,  Survival , and  Core : raise damage, shields, or pickup range, or mark purchases for automation; prices climb. Good—at least stardust has somewhere to go. Build Cannon, Plasma Orbs, Escort Drones, Scan Laser, Arc Generator, Missile Bay, Pulse Ring, and Ram Armor into eight distinct upgrade paths; Core keystones can change some of them. You do not get one bigger gun; you get a weapons bay too busy to stop firing.     A Crash Doesn't Repossess Your Stuff  Every 10 light-years brings one of six bosses: Planetary Fortress, Dreadnought, Hive Queen, Titan Meteor, Prism Sovereign, and Void Monolith, each with a bad habit. After a crash, return to the latest checkpoint and keep every upgrade, weapon unlock, and medal; first-time 10-light-year milestones award permanent medals boosting main-cannon damage and stardust income. Death does not reset progress; there is no prestige wipe. Pick Your Next Problem  After the  Tutorial Sector , choose among four sectors:    The Asteroid Belt : fewer enemies, no hazards.    The Comet Track : comet tails shove you around.    The Crystal Blight Corridor : denser waves, more elites, richer stardust.    The Void Ruins : more power-ups, but gravity anomalies pull you off course.  Switch among four Combat Doctrines: balanced  Cruise ,  Firepower  trading shields for damage,  Bulwark  trading damage for survival, or  Salvage  trading firepower for stardust and pickup range. Bestiary, Customization, and Coming Back  Six formations and six elite modifiers keep enemies changing. Log 41 enemy ships and bosses; Bestiary milestones at 8, 16, 26, and 41 entries grant permanent bonuses, as does completing each sector's exclusive set. The Stats page tracks deepest distance, kills, combos, and 22 in-game achievements; choose five ship designs and five engine-and-cannon theme colors, all cosmetic. After time away, the Voyage Report settles stardust; route progress and bosses still wait on the battlefield. A Quick Heads-Up  If you want a full-screen twin-stick shooter, a randomized build every run, or AI handling everything from minute one, this may not be your ship. It is a long-haul voyage at your desktop's edge: watch the firepower grow, then take the controls when things get dangerous.

about: You get on with your day. Your cat keeps climbing.  SummitJourney is a cozy idle climbing game with a cat companion. Choose a peak, route and supplies, then shrink the same journey into an always-on-top, transparent desktop-pet form. Your cat keeps you company in a corner while you do other things. Automatic hiking and offline progress continue the same journey.  Quiet company, with stories to return to  Choose Quiet company to enable auto-eating, camping, conservative event choices and Do Not Disturb. Your cat handles trail events while the mailbox and journey log keep the results for later. Repeat climbs remain your separate choice, and normal risks and failure outcomes still apply. Click the cat to open its panel, check finds or change settings.      A mountain in the corner of your desktop  Keep the hiking window beside whatever you are doing. Click to unfold the panel, check your hiker, and adjust automatic care. Close the panel when you are done, and let your cat carry on along the trail.             Take the scenic route  Hide the interface and settle into immersive mode. Follow your cat through forests and drifting clouds, up toward the snowline. The scenery changes with the mountain, altitude, and weather. Find a view you love, and take a photo to remember it.            Every climb starts with a packed bag  Check the altitude and estimated journey, then choose from six routes. How much food and water should you bring? What else will fit? Review your load, supplies, and risks before taking the first step.        A little rest goes a long way  Keep an eye on stamina, fullness, and mood. Eat along the way, make camp after dark, and recover before climbing on. Optional automatic feeding and night camping help you care for your hiker at your own pace.        Make the summit. Make it home.  Mark your arrival at the top, then follow the trail back down. Once safely at the foot of the mountain, look over your time, stars, and souvenirs. Another peak will be waiting when you are ready.             Someone left a little surprise  An item beside the trail. A few words for a stranger. Open a treasure left by another hiker, read their message, and perhaps find a small gift from their journey.        Leave something for the next hiker  Choose an item from your bag, write a short note, and leave it beside the path you have walked. Placing a treasure costs stamina. You can cancel before confirming, and choose exactly what you want to pass along.        Share a stretch of trail  A fellow hiker’s recorded climb may appear along your route. Walk beside their past footsteps for a while. These encounters are asynchronous, so a little company can find you even when you are not online together.             Remember who you meet  Record animal encounters in your field guide. Open an entry to see the illustration, affinity, and habitat, and get to know the creatures you might meet again on another climb.        Bring a little of the mountain home  Learn where herbs grow and what they do, then plan supplies for a future trip. Collect summit mementos with lasting bonuses, so the things you bring home can help you on the next trail.        Grow into the next climb  Spend earned funds on physical training and stars on permanent skills. Clear costs, levels, and progress help you build the abilities you need before setting out for a mountain you have been eyeing.        Dress for your next adventure  Browse the looks and outfits you have earned, and pick a favorite. Along with your growing collection and hard-earned skills, a new outfit makes this little hiker feel more like your own.              Ghost trails and treasures require an internet connection and contain asynchronous player content. Names and messages can be reported. Some GIFs use marked sample hikers and data; treasure discoveries do not always include a gift. Mountains, routes, and geography are stylized for the game.

about: A miniature world in a jar, right on your desktop  Saikei is the Japanese art of making miniature landscapes in a tray. This one comes in a glass jar that sits in the corner of your screen while you work, and it stays out of your way until you reach in.  Inside is a little world of grass, sand, stone and water. A river runs down from a spring, drops over waterfalls and empties into a turquoise lake. Through the glass you can see fish, seaweed and coral, and the layers of soil show along the side of the jar like an ant farm. Dig, pour, plant, build    Shovel:  dig bowls and plough trenches. The dirt piles up around the edges and settles into place.    Bucket:  pour streams of sand that pile into dunes.    Watering can:  fill hollows, flood channels and redirect the river. Running water carries sand downstream and carves its own paths.    Blocks:  lay grass and stone wherever you like.    Trees and buildings:  plant pines, round trees and red maples, or put down cottages, a pagoda, stone lanterns and torches.   Stop-motion clay Everything looks and moves like claymation, a little jerky and a little wobbly. Every block you place squashes and settles. The creatures move as if someone were nudging clay figures one frame at a time. A world that carries on without you    Crabs  scuttle sideways along the beach, snip their claws and run off with claws raised when you dig too close.    Fish  swim in loose schools, nibble seaweed and come straight over when you sprinkle food.    Octopuses  rest on the lake bed and jet away when startled.    Birds  perch on rooftops and treetops, loop around inside the jar and sometimes dive for a fish. They always miss.   The jar keeps your hours. The sun rises and sets when yours does, windows light up at dusk and fireflies come out at night. Every so often a rain shower rolls through, and the river and waterfalls run full. Made to sit there all day   Light on your computer, so you can leave it running.   Never interrupts what you're doing.   Pick a jar: rounded, round, oval or a tall bell jar, in large or small.   Every new jar holds a fresh world, and yours saves automatically.   No goals, no score, no way to lose.   Leave it in the corner and let it grow on you, or spend ten minutes digging a canal to see where the water goes.

Each happens once, and you are its only witness. Choose what your wallpaper shows    The whole galaxy.  A steady view from above, with every civilization's territory spread across the spiral arms.    The black hole.  The view from just above the accretion disk at the galaxy's centre, starlight bending around the shadow.    A star system. Stand on the ground and make that sky your desktop: the sun rises and sets about every twenty minutes.    A civilization's capital. Glance up between tasks: the wallpaper shows the year, the name of the age and the newest line of the observatory's log. Something worth reading happens about every half hour; a great power takes days to rise and fall.    Fly in.  Ctrl+Alt+G turns the wallpaper into a place you can move through: from the whole galaxy into any of 5,000 star systems, down to a planet, and onto its surface to watch the sun cross the sky. Idle on the desktop it draws ten frames a second on under 1% of the CPU, on integrated graphics, in a few hundred MB of memory. Planetary systems worked out from their star: habitable zones, giants beyond the snow line, multiple suns, white dwarfs, and tidally locked worlds whose people live in the twilight belt. short: You are a memory trafficker. Harvest stolen memories from captive minds and sell them to BRN CORP. Buy neural implants with your credits, but don't get addicted to your own supply, or you'll lose those memories forever. A shady cyberpunk idle game on your desktop.
about: **MEMORY DEALER**   You are a memory trafficker, street-level muscle in a cyberpunk economy that runs on other people's pasts. A captive brain glows in the corner of your desktop, and you sell what's inside it to BRN CORP, one memory at a time. The money is easy. Staying clean is not.          The Loop   Pulses drift across the brain. Tap one and a memory surfaces, paying you on the spot. Drop it into a slot and it sells itself to BRN CORP while you do something else. Commons pay slow and forever; Legendaries pay big and die fast. The skill is choosing what to run, and when to walk away.          Progression   Nothing here is infinite. Sell a memory dry and it refines, returning richer each time, and that gain never resets. Spend your credits on neural implants and upgrades, then wipe a spent brain to unlock the next: a new mind, a new past, a payout of Neurons for permanent upgrades that outlast every reset.         ### The Dealer's Brain   You can't stop using your own supply. The memories you've consumed start calling you back. RESIST costs cash, more every time. INDULGE costs nothing now and everything later: that memory is yours forever, jacked into your own skull, gone from the market, and its pulse rots into a phantom that drains your cash on sight. Your own brain fills in the same way, core by core, one glow for everyone you couldn't say no to.           ### Features     Always-on-top desktop widget that runs quietly while you work or browse    A procedural holographic brain rendered in real time: pure glowing neon visuals, zero art assets    5 unique brains, each a different person with a distinct look and a skewed spread of memories    119 memories sold to BRN CORP, from Commons worth pennies to Legendaries worth a fortune    Four upgrade paths competing for the same cash: HUSTLE (sale speed), HARVEST (pulse spawn rate), PIPELINE (queue depth and on-brain pulse cap), SCAN PROTOCOL (force-spawn a chosen rarity)    Permanent memory refinement: every memory grows more valuable with each extraction cycle, and the gains survive every wipe    Rapport streaks: sell the same memory on repeat and stack a growing bonus    The Dealer's Brain: resist your cravings at an escalating cash cost, or indulge and wire the memory into your own head forever as a cash-draining phantom    Neural implants and Neurons: permanent upgrades bought with your earnings that outlast every Memory Wipe    Fully localized in English, French, German, Spanish (LatAm), Brazilian Portuguese, and Simplified Chinese

Drag them anywhere on a free-form canvas, size them how you like, or hit  Arrange  and let Gamepan lay them out for you.  No ads interrupting you. No subscription draining your wallet every month. No account to make, no login to forget. You buy it once, it runs on your PC, and everything you make stays on your machine. One workspace, every game Build a layout that fits how  you  play, with unlimited tabs and modules, grouped into collapsible categories to keep big setups tidy. Whether it's an extraction shooter, a roguelike, a sprawling RPG, an MMO grind or a cozy farming sim, Gamepan adapts to the game, not the other way around.  And it isn't just for video games. It's great for  tabletop RPGs , too. Keep your campaign map, NPCs, loot, quest log and session journal in one place, then pull them up at the table on a phone or tablet with view-only sharing. 24 modules, mix and match Drop in exactly what a game needs:    Checklist and Kanban board:  quests, dailies, achievement hunts and long-term goals    Farming Tracker:  grind goals with checklist progress toward what you need    Map / Pins:  your own map images with pins, zones, categories and labels, from a small sketch to a huge world map    Items, Builds and Collection:  a catalog of your gear, loadouts with item links, and completion tracking    Crafting Calculator:  pick what to make and get the raw-material list, the in-between crafts and the total cost    Table, Stats and Counters:  gear, mats, NPCs, currency, deaths, runs, anything with a number    Timers and Calendar:  resets, respawns and raid nights, with alerts    Skill Tree:  plan talent and tech trees with prerequisites and a point budget    Notes and Session journal:  rich text, images, and a running diary of your sessions    Dashboard and Activity Log:  a live overview of everything, and a history of your changes    Spin the wheel, Dice roller and Coin flip:  let fate pick your next run, build or challenge    Whiteboard, Gallery and Links:  annotate screenshots, keep albums, and save your wikis and guides   Maps that are actually yours Upload any map image and make it useful: drop pins, draw zones, sort everything into color-coded categories, and filter what you see. Labels stay readable as you zoom, and big maps stay smooth. Use it for extraction routes, hidden collectibles, a dungeon you're mapping by hand, or the world of your D&D campaign. A companion that shows up A floating  overlay  keeps your modules on top of your game, live and interactive, so you can tick off a quest or check a map without alt-tabbing. Set its opacity, pick which modules it shows, and let Gamepan  auto-detect  when a game you've set up starts and open its overlay for you. Share it on the Steam Workshop Built something good? Put it on the Workshop and let other players use it. Publish a whole workspace, a single module or a map set, then browse, subscribe and import what everyone else has made, all without leaving the app. Publishing stays Private until you choose otherwise, and imported items go through a one-click safety review, so nothing loads unseen. Yours, and private Gamepan is  local-first . It has no account system and no tracking of any kind. Your workspaces live on your PC as plain files you fully control, so you can export them, back them up or wipe them anytime.  Sharing setups is safe, too. When you import a workspace from someone else, its images and links stay hidden behind a one-click review, so nothing unexpected loads until you say so. Anything you add yourself always shows. about: Somewhere in your computer, there is a creature nobody has met yet.   Kipple is a cosy desktop companion and creature collector for Windows. A little creature lives in a transparent, always-on-top window while you work, play or stare meaningfully at a spreadsheet. Your PC dreams its artwork locally, giving a small life its own appearance and personality.  It blinks. It reacts to a pet. It chats when you feel like company, remembers things you tell it, and counts electric sheep when it sleeps. Move it to a quiet corner, resize it, or let it take up rather more of your desk than you intended. A familiar creature. An unexpected combination.  Meet cute animals and unusual hybrids: a Foxguin, a Bunfrog, a Rambear, or another surprising little combination. Colours, silhouettes and expressions give your collection its character. Discover elemental Kipples with fire, ice, electric and earth effects that move around your companion.  Common, Rare, Pixel, Glitch, Mythic and Legendary are six visual tiers. Pixel creatures have a crisp sprite treatment; other rarities bring their own card styles and effects. Rarity changes the look, not competitive power. There is no PvP or power leaderboard. A little company, on your terms    Pet, chat with, move and resize your desktop companion.   Keep a collection and choose which Kipple joins you on the desktop.   Receive free drops while you play: Kipples, paints and boosters (details below).   Adjust text size and motion settings to make your companion comfortable to live with.   Your collection goes with Steam  Approved Kipples become persistent Steam inventory items, each with its own card showing the creature. Cards are still images; a Dream Reel animates one. Equipping a Kipple does not consume it: owning the item is owning the creature.  Keep your favourites or list eligible Kipples on the Steam Community Market. When one is sold, that creature moves to its new owner. Kipples, paints, boosters and Dream Reels use the Market rather than direct trades or gifting. Market access, holds and eligibility follow Steam's rules; availability and sale value are not guaranteed. Drops while you play  Kipple is free. While the game is open and signed in to Steam, your PC dreams drops: your first Kipple right away, then one drop every 12 hours of play. Pat, chat or emote with your Kipple once in each 3 hours of play and a drop takes 9 hours instead. Kipple's server counts the play time, up to 12 hours a day; time with the game closed does not count, and a ready drop waits until you claim it.  Each drop is a Kipple (20%), a paint (40%) or an item (40%):   Kipples: Common 92.89%, Rare 5%, Pixel 1%, Glitch 1%, Mythic 0.1%, Legendary 0.01%. 12% of Kipples carry an element: fire, electric, ice or earth, 3% each.   Paints: one of 372 colours and greys, each equally likely. A paint recolours a Kipple and is used up when applied; you see a preview first.   Items: Dream Incubator 64%, Dream Beacon 10%, Rarity Prism 10%, Element Spark 10%, Lucid Beacon 4%, Kipple Beacon 1%, Dream Reel 1%.   Boosters, Dream Reels and Fuse  Boosters are single-use Steam items that change your next drop:   Dream Incubator: takes 3 hours off the current drop.   Dream Beacon and Lucid Beacon: the next drop is a Kipple at least 50% or 75% of the time.   Kipple Beacon: the next drop is a Kipple; its rarity and element stay random.   Rarity Prism: doubles the chance of a non-Common Kipple on the next drop (7.11% to 14.22%).   Element Spark: doubles the chance of an element on the next drop (12% to 24%).  Different boosters combine, once each per drop. All activated boosters are spent on the next drop, even when it turns out to be a paint or an item.  A Dream Reel gives one of your Kipples an animated Steam card. The Kipple is re-made as an animated item: same creature, new card. about: YOU TYPE. HE FORGES. Brokk lives just above your taskbar, where he runs a forge and works whenever you do. You write emails or code, and he forges items. Every key you press brings his hammer down. When you type quickly, the furnace glows white-hot and Brokk gives it his all. When you take a break, he catches his breath too. A FORGE THAT KEEPS YOU GOING WITHOUT GETTING IN THE WAY The game is designed to stay out of the way while you work. Typing fuels the forge, and Brokk keeps pace with you. Open the panel when you want to buy an upgrade or check on the shop, then get back to what you were doing. You can move the forge, resize it, tone down the effects or turn off the sound. LEGENDS ARE FORGED FROM ORE It starts with ore, then ingots hammered out one by one, and finally a finished piece: a dagger, a cauldron, a horseshoe or whatever the shop's customers have ordered. Sometimes the metal gleams and something legendary takes shape: Szczerbiec. Excalibur. Mjolnir. There are 49 item patterns across five rarity levels. You can browse your collection in the display cabinet.          From everyday tools to legendary mithril treasures.  HIS WIFE BRYGIDA RUNS THE SHOP    Brygida sells whatever comes off the anvil. Some customers buy what's on the shelves. Others place special orders and pay extra. You decide how freely the forge spends on ore for new items, from inexpensive copper to the best metal you can afford.         THE FORGE PAYS FOR ITS OWN UPGRADES The gold you earn goes back into the forge and shop. Buy Brokk a heavier hammer or better bellows, and Brygida a new sign to bring in more customers. A whetstone improves your chances of forging rarer pieces, while counter decorations raise prices in the shop. You can speed up forging, increase earnings or save up for the next metal. Just leave some gold for ore.  As your equipment improves, the little workshop changes with it. You can also give the forge a different look by choosing a workshop style.         FROM COPPER TO MITHRIL Start with copper, then unlock bronze and iron. Keep building up your forge to work with steel, silver, gold and finally mithril. Each new metal gives you another reason to get back to the anvil, fill your collection and invest in your workshop. TRY THE FREE DEMO The demo lets you forge with copper, bronze and iron. If you choose, you can carry over your collection, forge and shop upgrades, and gathered resources when the full game is released.  Add My Desktop Dwarf: Taskbar Forge to your wishlist and follow the game to keep up with the forge.   Privacy:  The game counts key and mouse-button presses. It does not record the text you type. Gameplay works offline.

about: A little ocean that lives at the bottom of your screen.   Still Waters is a cozy idle aquarium that takes up residence at the bottom of your screen.  While you work, study, watch, game, doomscroll, or do absolutely nothing.  A small, living strip of water with fish, plants, and a quiet little ecosystem going about its day.  You can ignore it for hours and come back to find your fish thriving...  Or you can reach in and stir things up.   The aquarium you can actually reach into.   You know how, in real life, sticking your arm into an aquarium is generally frowned upon? Not here.    Grab any fish and drag it wherever you like    Toss them into the air and skim them across the surface    Collide them. Airborne fish bounce off each other and anything else that’s flying around    Make waves across the surface. Stir up sand from the floor.       Feed them by hand. They'll chase your cursor, sometimes leaping clean out of the water for a bite.    Toss them a beach ball. Drop an anchor. Rip kelp straight out of the seabed and spin it around like a windmill.  You decide how chaotic or chill it gets.   Somewhere new to drift.   Sunlit streams. Golden koi ponds. Tropical reefs bursting with color.   Frozen arctic waters. The depths below.  Each one with its own creatures and its own mood.  New places to discover as you go.    Fill your Fishipedia.   Some fish drift. Some dart. Some hide. Some hunt.   A growing roster of creatures to discover and collect - each with their own behaviors, moods, and quirks. Some traits come down to species. Some are just luck of the draw.  Buy eggs and wait to see what hatches...  Buy more of the fish you've already discovered...  Or create your own custom morphs and put something in the water that nobody else has.    No one expects you to oversee these waters alone.   You'll have a furry friend keeping you company.  Pet them. You can fish slowly, or you can carefully consider throwing the rod next time for a desired fish.   Leisurely hanging up, there are also worth pondering next steps   Let the character automatically fish and come back to check the fish basket during busy breaks. Sell fish catches to accumulate coins, purchase fishing equipment, and gradually challenge more substantial goals. Different fishing spots, fish species, and water layers require suitable bait and equipment; Find the right combination to add more anticipation to the wait.   Follow the fishing float to different places   From West Lake in Hangzhou to Lake Biwa, and then to distant lakes and wetlands, each stop has different scenery, fish species, and local commissions. Get to know the fish here and collect anecdotes that belong here, making each stop a memory on the journey.   Collect fish species and wait for unexpected surprises   Gradually light up the fish encyclopedia, break your weight record, and also pay attention to those rare and colorful fish. Accept the commission and ensure that every harvest has a destination   After receiving the local commission, newly caught fish that meet the conditions will be prioritized in the commission schedule, while other harvests can be arranged freely. name: Visualization for Steam with Arduino
lang: English
short: Visualization for Steam with Arduino is a PC software and Arduino firmware package for players who want to build a custom faceplate for their Steam Machine or Steam gaming PC. External hardware required.
about: Give your gaming setup a face of its own   Build a custom faceplate that brings your Steam games and system stats onto a physical display.  Visualization for Steam with Arduino combines a PC companion app and Arduino firmware for your Steam Machine or Steam gaming PC.   External hardware required. This purchase includes software and firmware only; no physical components or games are included.  Your game at a glance    See your active Steam user and currently running game.   Show game cover art and player and global achievement information where available.   Monitor FPS and CPU, GPU, RAM, and VRAM usage while you play.   Browse display pages with an Arduino Modulino Knob, Buttons, or Joystick.   Available metrics and achievement data depend on the game, system, drivers, and Steam data. Connect, customize, play  The app detects a supported Arduino board and installs the matching firmware when needed. A single USB cable powers the board and carries firmware and display data. The companion app runs quietly in the background and can be minimized to the system tray.  Build with off-the-shelf modules and solder-free Qwiic connections. Create your own faceplate, enclosure, and mounting layout, with reusable components and no battery required. What you need    Full display setup: Arduino UNO R4 Minima or UNO R4 WiFi, Adafruit 2.8-inch TFT Display Shield V2, four Arduino Modulino LED Matrix modules, and at least one Modulino Knob, Buttons, or Joystick.   Matrix-only setup: Arduino UNO R4 WiFi and four Modulino LED Matrix modules, without a TFT display or input module.   USB and suitable Qwiic cables, plus your own faceplate or mounting solution. Allow room for the electronics and preserve your PC's airflow.   Windows or Linux, including SteamOS, with the Steam client running and the board accessible as a USB serial device.   The official website (follow the link on the right panel) provides more product details, along with installation and configuration instructions to help you get started. Its gallery offers a closer look at the display and custom builds, while the changelog documents updates and improvements.
